Rashi on Sotah 3b:10:1.hebrew: ה"ג - ורבי ישמעאל, איידי דכתיב ״ובאחיכם״ כתיב נמי ״בהם״, כדתניא כו':
Rashi on Sotah 3b:10:1.english: Thus we read - "And Rabbi Yishmael: Since it is written, 'and among your brothers,' it is also written, 'among them,'" as it was taught [in a baraita], etc.

Rashi on Sotah 3b:11:1.hebrew: קריא - תולעת של שומשמין. האוכלתן, כך הזנות מחרבת את הבית:
Rashi on Sotah 3b:11:1.english: Kareya - A worm [found] in sesame seeds, which eats them; so too, licentiousness destroys the house.

Rashi on Sotah 3b:11:3.hebrew: אידי ואידי - תוקפא וזנותא, דאמרינן דמחרבת את הבית:
Rashi on Sotah 3b:11:3.english: Both this and that - the severity and the harlotry, of which we said that it destroys the house.

Rashi on Sotah 3b:11:4.hebrew: באיתתא - כשהאשה מזנה או כעסנית, לפי שהאשה מתעסקת בזנוניה ואינה עושה מלאכתה ולא משמרת ביתה, ומפקרת את של בעלה למנאפים:
Rashi on Sotah 3b:11:4.english: In a woman - When the woman is promiscuous or irascible. For the woman busies herself with her licentiousness and does not do her work or watch over her house, and she abandons her husband's property to adulterers.

Rashi on Sotah 3b:12:1.english: Before Israel sinned - with [forbidden] sexual relations.

Rashi on Sotah 3b:12:2.english: With each and every one - In his house.

Rashi on Sotah 3b:12:3.hebrew: נסתלקה מהם - מלבא לביתם, דאינו יכול לראות בעבירות שבביתו:
Rashi on Sotah 3b:12:3.english: It departed from them - From coming to their home, for [the Divine Presence] cannot see the transgressions in its home.

Rashi on Sotah 3b:13:1.english: Precedes him - Before his death, it proclaims [his merit] before him.

Rashi on Sotah 3b:13:2.english: Wraps around him - She winds herself around him.

Rashi on Sotah 3b:15:1.hebrew: תנן התם - בפ' מי שקינא (לקמן סוטה לא.) אמאי דקתני אמר עד אחד ראיתיה שנטמאה, לא היתה שותה:
Rashi on Sotah 3b:15:1.english: We learned there - In ch. "Mi She'kinei" (below, Sotah 31a), regarding that which it teaches: If one witness said, "I saw her, that she became defiled," she does not drink:

Rashi on Sotah 3b:15:2.hebrew: שהיה בדין - שלא להאמינו, אי לאו דכתיב קרא:
Rashi on Sotah 3b:15:2.english: For it would have been logical - not to believe him, were it not that a verse is written.

Rashi on Sotah 3b:16:1.english: The first - [This refers to] the *seterah* (the seclusion of the woman with another man after her husband's warning).

Rashi on Sotah 3b:16:2.hebrew: אין אוסרתה איסור עולם - שאם תשתה ותמצא טהורה, מותרת לבעלה ולתרומה:
Rashi on Sotah 3b:16:2.english: It does not forbid her with a permanent prohibition - For if she drinks and is found pure, she is permitted to her husband and to terumah.

Rashi on Sotah 3b:16:3.hebrew: אין מתקיימת בפחות משנים - כדבעינן למיגמר דבר דבר מממון:
Rashi on Sotah 3b:16:3.english: It is not upheld with fewer than two - As we need to derive [it] by verbal analogy ("davar davar") from monetary law.

Rashi on Sotah 3b:16:4.english: The latter - The impurity that comes after the seclusion.

Rashi on Sotah 3b:17:1.hebrew: כל שיש בה - כל עדות שיש בה נאמן, כדדרשינן לעיל: ״ועד אין בה״ — תרי אלא חד. וקא אמר אסורה, ואטומאה קאי, דהא מינה סליק: ״והיא נטמאה ועד אין בה״:
Rashi on Sotah 3b:17:1.english: Whatever is in her - Any testimony that is in her is believed, as we expounded above: "and there is no witness in her" — [meaning that the witnesses need] not [be] two, but [even] one. And [the Tanna] says she is forbidden, and he is referring to the defilement, for it is derived from there: "and she was defiled, and there is no witness in her."

Rashi on Sotah 3b:18:1.english: An a fortiori argument - That [the first testimony] should be established by a single witness.

Rashi on Sotah 3b:19:1.hebrew: תלמוד לומר - באשה מקלקלת, "כי מצא בה ערות דבר", ולהלן (סוטה כו':):
Rashi on Sotah 3b:19:1.english: Scripture states - Regarding a woman who acts improperly, "for he found in her an indecent matter" (Deuteronomy 24:1), and below (Sotah 26b) ...

Rashi on Sotah 3b:19:2.hebrew: ופרכינן: למה לי למיכתב? למילפה בגזירה שוה!
Rashi on Sotah 3b:19:2.english: And we challenge: Why do I need it to be written? It could be derived through a *gezerah shavah*!

Rashi on Sotah 3b:1:1.hebrew: אם כן - דלאו לחובה אתא, אלא להך דרשא:
Rashi on Sotah 3b:1:1.english: If so - For it does not come [to teach] an obligation, but rather for this derivation.

Rashi on Sotah 3b:1:2.hebrew: לכתוב רחמנא לה ולשתוק - דמשמע: "לנפש לא יטמא בעמיו, כי אם לשארו" וגו' "ולאחותו הבתולה" — "לה", כלומר לגופה שלם, ולא לאיבריה:
Rashi on Sotah 3b:1:2.english: Let the Merciful One write "for her" and be silent - For it would imply: "For a [dead] person he shall not defile himself among his people, except for his relative," etc., "and for his virgin sister" — "for her," meaning for her whole body, but not for her limbs.

Rashi on Sotah 3b:20:1.hebrew: בה ולא בקינוי כו' מיבעי ליה - דכיון דכתיב בה, מיעוטא הוא, ולא גמרי' שאר עדיות דאשה מינה, וקמו להו במלתייהו ככל עדיות שבתורה:
Rashi on Sotah 3b:20:1.english: "In her," and not "in warning," etc. – it should have said - For since it is written "in her," it is a limiting term [that excludes]. And we do not derive the other testimonies concerning a woman from it, and they stand in their place, like all testimonies in the Torah.

Rashi on Sotah 3b:21:1.hebrew: הכי נמי קאמר - וגזירה שוה למילתא אחריתי נקט, ומתניתין חסורי מיחסרא, והכי תנא ליה: ת"ל "בה" — ולא בקינוי וסתירה; וגזירה שוה לטומאת אשה דעלמא, שלא קינא לה בעלה, ובא עד אחד ואמר: אני ראיתיה שנטמאה, דלא מהימן. והכא הוא דמהימן, משום דרגלים לדבר:
Rashi on Sotah 3b:21:1.english: So too, he is saying - And [the Mishnah] took the verbal analogy (gezeirah shavah) for a different matter; and the Mishnah is lacking [something], and this is what it taught: The verse states "in her" — [meaning] and not through warning and seclusion. And [it takes] the verbal analogy for the impurity of an ordinary woman, whose husband did not warn her, and one witness came and said, "I saw that she became impure," [in which case] he is not believed. But here he is believed, because there is circumstantial evidence (lit., "the feet of the matter").

Rashi on Sotah 3b:4:1.hebrew: לא תחיה כל נשמה - בשבעה אומות כתיב: החתי והגרגשי והאמורי והכנעני והפריזי והחוי והיבוסי:
Rashi on Sotah 3b:4:1.english: You shall not let any soul live - [This] is written regarding the seven nations: the Hittite, the Girgashite, the Amorite, the Canaanite, the Perizzite, the Hivite, and the Jebusite.

Rashi on Sotah 3b:4:2.hebrew: למשרי אחד מן האומות - משאר שבעים אומות:
Rashi on Sotah 3b:4:2.english: To permit one of the nations - from the other seventy nations.

Rashi on Sotah 3b:4:3.hebrew: שבא על הכנענית - כל שבע אומות נקראו על שם כנען:
Rashi on Sotah 3b:4:3.english: Who had relations with a Canaanite woman - All seven nations are called by the name of Canaan.

Rashi on Sotah 3b:4:4.hebrew: והוליד בן - דהלך אחר האב, ומותר להחיותו לך לעבד:
Rashi on Sotah 3b:4:4.english: And he fathered a son - For [the child] follows the father, and it is permitted to keep him alive for you as a slave.

Rashi on Sotah 3b:5:1.english: For it was taught - That it is for this [purpose] that the verse came.

Rashi on Sotah 3b:5:2.english: With a slave - We read [this] with a bet.

Rashi on Sotah 3b:5:3.hebrew: וגם מבני התושבים וגו' - לעיל מיניה כתיב: "מאת הגוים אשר סביבותיכם, מהם תקנו עבד ואמה", אשר סביבות ארצכם, ולא מבני ארצכם דשבעה אומות. "וגם מבני התושבים" — כל תושב היינו שבא ממקום אחר ונתיישב כאן, וקאמר קרא שמותר לקנות מבניהם אשר יהיו להם מבנות ארצך:
Rashi on Sotah 3b:5:3.english: "And also from the children of the residents," etc. - In the preceding verse it is written: "From the nations that are around you, from them you may acquire a slave and a maidservant" — [meaning those] around your land, and not from the people of your land, of the seven nations. "And also from the children of the residents" — any "resident" [toshav] is one who came from another place and settled here; and the verse is saying that it is permitted to acquire from their children, who were born to them from the daughters of your land.

Rashi on Sotah 3b:6:1.hebrew: מן הנולדים בארצכם - בנים הנולדים בארצכם, והם בני התושבים, דהיינו אחרים שנשאו בארצכם נשים — אתה רשאי לקנות:
Rashi on Sotah 3b:6:1.english: From those born in your land - Children born in your land, who are the children of the residents — that is, of others who married women in your land — you are permitted to buy.

Rashi on Sotah 3b:6:2.hebrew: ולא מן הגרים בארצכם - ולא מן הבנים הנולדים לבני ארצכם במקום אחר, מבנות שאר אומות, והביאום לבניהם לגור שם:
Rashi on Sotah 3b:6:2.english: And not from those who dwell in your land - And not from the children born to the people of your land in another place, from daughters of other nations, whom they then brought to their sons to dwell there.

Rashi on Sotah 3b:8:1.english: And not in your brethren - [This refers to] the labor of a slave.

Tosafot on Sotah 3b:17:1.hebrew: ת"ל ועד אין בה כל שיש בה - תימה: כיון דהוא קינא לה ונסתרה, והשתא אתי עד א' דטומאה, מסתמא בעל שתיק ולא מכחיש ליה — א"כ מאי צריך קרא דעד אחד נאמן? אפילו טומאה בעלמא בלא קנוי וסתירה בכי האי גוונא היה מהימן, כדאיתא בפרק האומר (קידושין דף סו.): אשתו זינתה בעד אחד וכו'. תינח לרבא דאמר התם הוה דבר שבערוה; אלא לאביי דאמר מהימן, מאי איכא למימר? אלא ע"כ אית לן למימר דלאביי לא איצטריך קרא אלא היכא דמכחיש, אע"ג דקינא לה:
Tosafot on Sotah 3b:17:1.english: 'Scripture states: "and there is no witness in her" — [meaning] whatever has [a witness] in it' - This is surprising: Since he (the husband) warned her and she secluded herself, and now one witness comes [to testify] about impurity, presumably the husband would remain silent and not contradict him. If so, why is a verse needed [to teach] that one witness is believed? Even in a case of mere impurity, without a warning and without seclusion, he would be believed in such a situation, as stated in the chapter 'HaOmer' (Kiddushin 66a): [If a man says,] 'My wife committed adultery,' [he is believed] on the word of one witness, etc. This works according to Rava, who said there that it is a 'matter of ervah' [and therefore requires two witnesses, so the verse is needed here to permit one]; but according to Abaye, who said that [one witness] is believed, what can be said? Rather, we must necessarily say that according to Abaye, the verse is needed only where [the husband] contradicts [the witness], even though he warned her.

Tosafot on Sotah 3b:18:1.hebrew: מה עדות אחרונה שאוסרתה איסור עולם - תימה: דהוה מצי למפרך, מה לעדות האחרונה שכן רגלים לדבר, שהרי קינא לה ונסתרה:
Tosafot on Sotah 3b:18:1.english: "Just as the latter testimony, which prohibits her forever" - This is puzzling: for [the Gemara] could have refuted [the *kal vachomer*] by saying, "What is [the stringency] of the latter testimony? [It is that] there is a basis for the matter [*raglayim ladavar*], since [the husband] had warned her and she had secluded herself [with the man]."

Tosafot on Sotah 3b:1:1.hebrew: ורבי עקיבא א"כ לכתוב לה - תימה: לרב חסדא דאמר בפרק שלשה מינין (נזיר דף מג:): "לאביו" בזמן שהוא שלם, ולא בזמן שהוא לאיברים — לדידיה לא איצטריך "לה" לאיברים, מאי הוי? דריש ב"לה יטמא". ויש לומר: הוה דריש לחובה כדרבי עקיבא, ואיידי דכתב "יטמא" כתב "לה":
Tosafot on Sotah 3b:1:1.english: "And Rabbi Akiva: If so, let [the Torah] write 'lah' (for her)" - This is puzzling according to Rav Chisda, who said in the chapter Shelosha Minin (Nazir 43b) [that the phrase] "for his father" [applies] when [the corpse] is whole, but not when it is [only] limbs. According to him, [the word] "lah" was not needed [to teach about] limbs, so what of it? He could expound [it from] "lah yitama" ([a priest] may defile himself for her). And one can say: He would expound it [as teaching] an obligation, like Rabbi Akiva, and since [the Torah] wrote "yitama," it wrote "lah."

Tosafot on Sotah 3b:22:1.hebrew: נאמר כאן דבר ונאמר להלן דבר - תימה: למה לי ג"ש? אפילו בלא ג"ש, מהיכא תיתי ליה דלית הימן בה עד אחד? מעדות אחרונה ליכא למילף, דאיכא פירכא:
Tosafot on Sotah 3b:22:1.english: "A 'matter' (davar) is stated here, and a 'matter' is stated there" - This is puzzling: why do I need a *gezerah shavah* (verbal analogy)? Even without a *gezerah shavah*, from where would we get [the idea] that one witness is not believed regarding her? One cannot derive it from the latter testimony, since there is a refutation.

Tosafot on Sotah 3b:4:1.hebrew: למשרי אחד מכל האומות - מהכא נפקא לן דבאומות הלך אחר הזכר:
Tosafot on Sotah 3b:4:1.english: To permit [marriage with] one from any of the nations - From here we derive that regarding the nations, one follows the male.

Tosafot on Sotah 3b:8:1.hebrew: כתיב נמי (ובאחיכם) לכדתנא דבי רבי ישמעאל - וא"ת: הא אצטריך, דדרשינן בפרק איזהו נשך (ב"מ דף עג:): מנין אם ראיתו נוהג שלא כשורה שאתה רשאי להשתעבד בו וכו'. וי"ל: אסמכתא בעלמא הוא, וקנס חכמים הוא כדי לייסרן:
Tosafot on Sotah 3b:8:1.english: It is also written ("and over your brethren") [to teach] like [the teaching of] the Tanna of the school of Rabbi Yishmael - And if you ask: But [this verse] is needed, for we expound in the chapter "Eizehu Neshekh" (Bava Metzia 73b): From where [do we derive] that if you saw him [your Jewish slave] behaving improperly, you are permitted to enslave him [i.e., to work him as a slave], etc.? And one can answer: It is merely an asmakhta (a textual support), and it is a penalty [imposed] by the Sages in order to discipline them.
